WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
Jeroboam "fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon". 1 Kings 11:40
"In the fifth year of king Rehoboam ... Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem" and took the treasures of the temple and the palace and Solomon's shields of gold. 1 Kings 14:25–26

Chronicles: he came "because they had transgressed against the LORD", with twelve hundred chariots, sixty thousand horsemen and peoples without number: "the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians". 2 Chronicles 12:2–3
Shemaiah: "Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak." 2 Chronicles 12:5
When Judah humbled itself, the LORD said his wrath would not be poured out "by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless they shall be his servants". 2 Chronicles 12:7–8
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Chronicles ties the invasion to Rehoboam's forsaking "the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him". 2 Chronicles 12:1–2
The king and princes humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous". 2 Chronicles 12:6
Rehoboam replaced Solomon's gold shields with brass. 1 Kings 14:27
Jeroboam, fleeing Solomon, went to Shishak and stayed in Egypt until Solomon's death. 1 Kings 11:40
Judah was to serve Shishak, "that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries". 2 Chronicles 12:8
His army brought "the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians" (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 12:3

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No regnal years. Scripture dates his invasion only by Rehoboam's fifth year (1 Kgs 14:25; 2 Chr 12:2).
HORNUNG, KRAUSS AND WARBURTON (2006), FOR SHOSHENQ I
BREASTED (1906), FOR SHOSHENQ I
Chronological table: "21 (+0?) years 945–924 B.C." He dates the campaign "probably about 926 B.C." (vol. IV §709).
T. NICOL, ISBE (1915), FOR SHOSHENQ I
Probably about 926 BC
J. H. Breasted (1906)
Breasted places the campaign in Rehoboam's fifth year, "probably about 926 B.C.", in the latter half of Shoshenq's reign, before the year-21 building that carried its relief. 1 Kings 14:25 [4]
About 926/925 BC
Rehoboam's fifth year on McFall's revision of Thiele (1991)
McFall's table starts Rehoboam in 931/930 BC, so Rehoboam's fifth year, when Scripture puts the invasion, falls about 926/925 BC. 1 Kings 14:25 2 Chronicles 12:2 [31]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say why Shishak sheltered Jeroboam.
Scripture does not say that Shishak fought for Jerusalem; both books say he "came up against Jerusalem" and took its treasures.
Scripture names none of the fenced cities he took.
None of the Egyptian records used for this page names Rehoboam or Jeroboam.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

Scholars' viewShishak is identified with Shoshenq I, founder of Egypt's 22nd dynasty. Champollion, reading the Karnak relief in 1828, wrote that the identity he had proposed was confirmed there; Breasted (1906) and Nicol (1915) follow it. 1 Kings 14:25 [8][4][14]
